verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              यदि घोरं समुद्दिष्टमश्रद्धेयमिवानृतम् । अस्मि स्विद्दस्युमर्यादा यामहं परिवर्जये ॥१॥
verses.english: That which is without qualities, O son, can never be explained by assigning qualities to it. Listen, however, to me as I explain to you what is endued with qualities and what is devoid of them.

verses.sanskrit: सम्मुह्यामि विषीदामि धर्मो मे शिथिलीकृतः । उद्यमं नाधिगच्छामि कदाचित्परिसान्त्वयन् ॥२॥
verses.english: Great Munis conversant with the truth about principles say that when Soul seizes qualities like a crystal catching the reflection of a red flower, he is said to be possessed of qualities; but when freed from qualities like the crystal freed from reflection, he is seen in his real nature, which is as above all qualities.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              नैतच्छ्रुत्वाऽऽगमादेव तव धर्मानुशासनम् । प्रजासमवहारोऽयं कविभिः सम्भृतं मधु ॥३॥
verses.english: Unmanifest Nature is by her nature endued with qualities. She cannot transcends them. Shorn of intelligence by nature she becomes attached to qualities.

verses.sanskrit: बह्व्यः प्रतिविधातव्याः प्रज्ञा राज्ञा ततस्ततः । नैकशाखेन धर्मेण यत्रैषा सम्प्रवर्तते ॥४॥
verses.english: Unmanifest Nature cannot know anything, while Purusha, by his nature, is endued with knowledge.—There is nothing higher than myself, the Soul is always conscious of it.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्धिसंजननो धर्म आचारश्च सतां सदा । ज्ञेयो भवति कौरव्य सदा तद्विद्धि मे वचः ॥५॥
verses.english: Therefore the unmanifest Nature, although by nature inanimate and unintelligent, still becomes animate and intelligent on account of her union with the Soul who is Eternal and Indestructible instead of remaining in her own nature owing to her destructibility.

verses.sanskrit: बुद्धिश्रेष्ठा हि राजानश्चरन्ति विजयैषिणः । धर्मः प्रतिविधातव्यो बुद्ध्या राज्ञा ततस्ततः ॥६॥
verses.english: When Soul, through ignorance, repeatedly becomes associated with qualities, he fails to understand his own real nature and therefore he fails to acquire Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: नैकशाखेन धर्मेण राज्ञो धर्मो विधीयते । दुर्बलस्य कुतः प्रज्ञा पुरस्तादनुपाहृता ॥७॥
verses.english: On account of the Soul's Supremacy over the principles that originate from Nature he is said to partake of the nature of those principles. On account also of his agency in the matter of creation, he is said to possess the quality of creation. On account of his agency in the matter of Yoga, he is said to possess the quality of Yoga. For his Supremacy over those particular principles know by the name of Nature, he is said to possess the character of Nature.

verses.sanskrit: अद्वैधज्ञः पथि द्वैधे संशयं प्राप्तुमर्हति । बुद्धिद्वैधं वेदितव्यं पुरस्तादेव भारत ॥८॥
verses.english: For his agency in the matter of creating the seeds, he is said to partake of the nature of those seeds. And because he causes the several principles or qualities to come into being, he is, therefore, said to be subject to decay and destruction.

verses.sanskrit: पार्श्वतः करणं प्राज्ञो विष्टंभित्वा प्रकारयेत् । जनस्तच्चरितं धर्मं विजानात्यन्यथान्यथा ॥९॥
verses.english: On account, again, of his being the witness of everything, and on account, also of there being nothing else than he, as also for his consciousness of oneness with Nature, Yatis endued with ascetic success, conversant with the spiritual science, and freed from fever of every sort, consider him as existing by himself without a second, immutable, unmanifest, unstable, and manifest.

verses.sanskrit: अमिथ्याज्ञानिनः केचिन्मिथ्याविज्ञानिनः परे । तद्वै यथायथं बुद्ध्वा ज्ञानमाददते सताम् ॥१०॥
verses.english: This is what we have heard. Those Sankhyas, however, that depend upon Knowledge only and the practice of mercy for all creatures, say that it is Nature which is Ore but souls are many.

verses.sanskrit: परिमुष्णन्ति शास्त्राणि धर्मस्य परिपन्थिनः । वैषम्यमर्थविद्यानां निरर्थाः ख्यापयन्ति ते ॥११॥
verses.english: As a matter of fact, Soul is different from Nature which though unstable, still appears as stable. As a blade of reed is different from its outer cover, so is Soul different from Nature.

verses.sanskrit: आजिजीविषवो विद्यां यशःकामौ समन्ततः । ते सर्वे नृप पापिष्ठा धर्मस्य परिपन्थिनः ॥१२॥
verses.english: Indeed, the worm that lies within the Udumvara should be known as different from the Udumvara, Though existing with the Udumvara, the worm is not to be considered as forming a part of the Udumvara.

verses.sanskrit: अपक्वमतयो मन्दा न जानन्ति यथातथम् । यथा ह्यशास्त्रकुशलाः सर्वत्रायुक्तिनिष्ठिताः ॥१३॥
verses.english: The fish is separate from the water in which it lives, and the water is separate from the fish that lives in it. Though the fish and water exist together, yet it is never drenched by water.

verses.sanskrit: परिमुष्णन्ति शास्त्राणि शास्त्रदोषानुदर्शिनः । विज्ञानमर्थं विद्यानां न सम्यगिति वर्तते ॥१४॥
verses.english: The fire that lies in an earthen saucepan is separate from the earthen saucepan, and the saucepan is separate from the fire it contains. although the fire exists in and with the saucepan, yet it is not to be considered as constituting any part of it.

verses.sanskrit: निन्दया परविद्यानां स्वविद्यां ख्यापयन्ति च । वागस्त्रा वाक्छरीभूता दुग्धविद्याफला इव ॥१५॥
verses.english: The lotus-leaf that lies afloat on a piece of water is separate from the piece of water on which it floats. Because it exists with water it does not form a portion of the water.

verses.sanskrit: तान्विद्यावणिजो विद्धि राक्षसानिव भारत । व्याजेन सद्भिर्विहितो धर्मस्ते परिहास्यति ॥१६॥
verses.english: The eternal existence of those objects in and with those mentioned, is never correctly understood by ordinary mortals.

verses.sanskrit: न धर्मवचनं वाचा नैव बुद्ध्येति नः श्रुतम् । इति बार्हस्पतं ज्ञानं प्रोवाच मघवा स्वयम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: They who see Nature and Soul in any other light are said to possess an incorrect vision. It is certain that they have repeatedly to sink into dreadful hell.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वेव वचनं किंचिदनिमित्तादिहोच्यते । सुविनीतेन शास्त्रेण न व्यवस्यन्त्यथापरे ॥१८॥
verses.english: I have thus told you the philosophy of the Sankhyas, that excellent science by which all things have been correctly determined. Ascertaining the nature of Soul and Nature in this way, the Sankhyas acquire Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: लोकयात्रामिहैके तु धर्मं प्राहुर्मनीषिणः । समुद्दिष्टं सतां धर्मं स्वयमूहेत पण्डितः ॥१९॥
verses.english: I have also told of the systems of those others who are conversant with the great principles of the universe. I shall now describe to you the science of the Yogins,

verses.sanskrit: अमर्षाच्छास्त्रसम्मोहादविज्ञानाच्च भारत । शास्त्रं प्राज्ञस्य वदतः समूहे यात्यदर्शनम् ॥२०॥
verses.english: If even a wise man speaks of morality when he is angry or bewildered or ignorant, his speech produces no effect.

verses.sanskrit: आगतागमया बुद्ध्या वचनेन प्रशस्यते । अज्ञानाज्ज्ञानहेतुत्वाद्वचनं साधु मन्यते ॥२१॥
verses.english: Discourses on morality made with the help of an intelligent understanding of the true letter and spirit of the scriptures, should be lauded and not those which are made with the help of anything else. Sensible words, even if heard from an ignorant person, are regarded as pious and wise.

verses.sanskrit: अनया हतमेवेदमिति शास्त्रमपार्थकम् । दैतेयानुशना प्राह संशयच्छेदनं पुरा ॥२२॥
verses.english: In days of yore, Ushanas said to the Daityas this truth, which dispels all doubts, that scriptures are no scriptures if they cannot stand the crucible test of reason.

verses.sanskrit: ज्ञानमप्यपदिश्यं हि यथा नास्ति तथैव तत् । तं तथा छिन्नमूलेन सन्नोदयितुमर्हसि ॥२३॥
verses.english: The possession or absence of doubtful, knowledge is the same thing. You should root out and drive off such knowledge.

verses.sanskrit: अनव्यवहितं यो वा नेदं वाक्यमुपाश्नुते । उग्रायैव हि सृष्टोऽसि कर्मणे न त्वमीक्षसे ॥२४॥
अङ्ग मामन्ववेक्षस्व राजन्याय बुभूषते । यथा प्रमुच्यते त्वन्यो यदर्थं न प्रमोदते ॥२५॥
verses.english: See me, O dear child, how, by following the duties of my own order, I have sent innumerable Kshatriyas to heaven! There are some who are not pleased with me for this.

verses.sanskrit: अजोऽश्वः क्षत्रमित्येतत् सदृशं ब्रह्मणा कृतम् । तस्मादभीक्ष्णं भूतानां यात्रा काचित्प्रसिद्ध्यति ॥२६॥
verses.english: Goat, horse, and Kshatriya, were created by Brahman for the same purpose (of being useful to everybody). A Kshatriya, therefore, should always seek the happiness of all creatures.

verses.sanskrit: यस्त्ववध्यवधे दोषः स वध्यस्यावधे स्मृतः । या चैव खलु मर्यादा यामयं परिवर्जयेत् ॥२७॥
verses.english: The sin of killing a person unworthy of being killed is tantamount to that which is incurred by not killing one who deserves to be killed. Such is the established order of things which a weak-minded king never thinks of attending to.

verses.sanskrit: तस्मात्तीक्ष्णः प्रजा राजा स्वधर्मे स्थापयेत्ततः । अन्योन्यं भक्षयन्तो हि प्रचरेयुर्वृका इव ॥२८॥
verses.english: Therefore, a king should force all his subjects to observe their respective duties. If this is not done, they will prowl like wolves, devouring one another,

verses.sanskrit: यस्य दस्युगणा राष्ट्रे ध्वांक्षा मत्स्यान् जलादिव । विहरन्ति परस्वानि स वै क्षत्रियपांसनः ॥२९॥
verses.english: He is a wretch among Kshatriyas in whose kingdom robbers go about pillaging the property of other people like crows taking little fishes from water.

verses.sanskrit: कुलीनान् सचिवान् कृत्वा वेदविद्यासमन्वितान् । प्रशाधि पृथिवीं राजन् प्रजा धर्मेण पालयन् ॥३०॥
verses.english: Appointing high-born men with Vedic knowledge as your ministers, do you govern the Earth, protecting your subjects piously.

verses.sanskrit: विहीनं कर्मणा न्यायं यः प्रगृह्णाति भूमिपः । उपायस्याविशेषज्ञं तद्वै क्षत्रं नपुंसकम् ॥३१॥
verses.english: That Kshatriya who, innocent of the established customs and contrivances, improperly taxes his people, is considered as a eunuch of his order.

verses.sanskrit: नैवोग्रं नैव चानुग्रं धर्मेणेह प्रशस्यते । उभयं न व्यतिक्रामेदुग्रो भूत्वा मृदुर्भव ॥३२॥
verses.english: A king should neither be severe nor mild. If he rules fairly he deserves praise. A king should not renounce both that qualities; on the other hand, becoming severe when (it is necessary), he should be mild when it is necessary to be so.

verses.sanskrit: कष्टः क्षत्रियधर्मोऽयं सौहृदं त्वयि मे स्थितम् । उग्रकर्मणि सृष्टोऽसि तस्माद्राज्यं प्रशाधि वै ॥३३॥
verses.english: The observance of Kshatriya duties is highly difficult. I love you greatly. You are created for the performance of severe acts. Therefore, do you rule kingdom.

verses.sanskrit: अशिष्टनिग्रहो नित्यं शिष्टस्य परिपालनम् । एवं शुक्रोऽब्रवीद्धीमानापत्सु भरतर्षभ ॥३४॥
verses.english: The highly intelligent Shakra has said that in times of distress the great duty of a king is to punish the wicked and protect the good.

verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              अस्ति चेदिह मर्यादा यामन्यो नाभिलंघयेत् । पृच्छामि त्वां सतां श्रेष्ठ तन्मे ब्रूहि पितामह ॥३५॥
verses.english: Yudhishthira said Is there any such rule (regarding royal duties) which should, under no circumstances) be violated? I ask you this, O foremost of virtuous persons! Tell me, O grandfather.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              ब्राह्मणानेव सेवेत विद्यावृद्धास्तपस्विनः । श्रुतचारित्रवृत्ताढ्यान्पवित्रं ह्येतदुत्तमम् ॥३६॥
verses.english: Bhishma said One should always adore Brahmanas respected for learning, devoted to penances, and observant of Vedic injunctions. This, indeed, is a high and sacred duty.

verses.sanskrit: या देवतासु वृत्तिस्ते साऽस्तु विप्रेषु नित्यदा । क्रुद्धैर्हि विप्रैः कर्माणि कृतानि बहुधा नृप ॥३७॥
verses.english: You should always treat the Brahmanas like the gods. The Brahmanas, if enraged, can inflict pains in a variety of ways, O King.

verses.sanskrit: प्रीत्या यशो भवेन्मुख्यमप्रीत्या परमं भयम् । प्रीत्या ह्यमृतवद्विप्राः क्रुद्धाश्चैव विषं यथा ॥३८॥
verses.english: If they be pleased, you will win high fame. If otherwise, great will be your fear. If pleased, the Brahmanas become like ambrosia. If enraged, they become like poison.
